glosses: A collection, sometimes hidden; a reserve.

examples.text: They had quite a stash of food saved up for emergencies.

glosses: A place where drugs are stored.

examples.text: The dealers managed to store the dope in the stash just in time to avoid being caught by the police.

glosses: Clothing or other items branded with a particular university club or society's logo.

examples.text: We've now ordered stash for everyone who said they wanted some.

glosses: A collection of yarn or other materials not yet allocated to any particular craft project.

examples.text: My stash is mostly unfinished objects on the needles. I have one bag of yarn that I bought to make a coat.

glosses: To hide or store away for later use.

examples.text: He stashed his liquor in the cabinet under the bar.
“Landlord,” said I, “tell him to stash his tomahawk there, or pipe, or whatever you call it; tell him to stop smoking, in short, and I will turn in with him.

To save or keep (something) to be used at a later time.

examples.text: I try to put a few dollars aside each week, just in case I need money in an emergency.

glosses: To ignore or intentionally disregard (something), temporarily or permanently, so that more important things can occupy one's attention.

examples.text: Let's put our differences aside for the moment, and get this project finished.
Stanmore: Plans to provide step-free access to the Jubilee Line station have been put aside, after the housing development on the car park that would have paid for it was withdrawn.
